articles.title: Child safety groups urge Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys until proved safe
articles.summary: Advocates from across the world voice concern over privacy issues and inappropriate communication to children. More than 150 child safety groups and experts across six continents have urged Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys this Christmas until they are proved to be safe.
body: In a letter sent to Amazon’s president, Andy Jassy, and eBay’s president, Jamie Iannone, the coalition called for the online retailers to stop the sale of AI toys and offer refunds to customers who have already bought one.
The coalition, which includes the psychologist Jonathan Haidt’s The Anxious Generation Movement and UK and US child safety groups, says the risks associated with these toys are “well documented”.
The listing was pulled by Amazon, but after 48 hours the toy returned to the platform under a new retailer, according to Alliance 4 Children. The second listing has now been removed by Amazon.
“These toys are cheap, easy to buy and largely untested,” the letter stated, also noting that they were marketed towards children as young as three years old.
points: Advocates from across the world voice concern over privacy issues and inappropriate communication to children.

articles.title: How freaked out should we be? After mass outages, experts tell us how close we are to ‘doomsday’
articles.summary: As tech, travel and banking failures sweep the US, analysts and cyber-security directors discuss AI, underfunding and what keeps them up at night. Grounded flights. Bank websites crashing. Microsoft Outlook outages grinding business operations to a halt. Zoom, Ikea, and PokerStars websites hacked.
body: Even those who aren’t prone to conspiracy theories have been wondering out loud if these recent disruptions are somehow connected. Speculation runs wild about targeted cyber-attacks by Iranian hackers, or AI agents autonomously hacking critical (air traffic, banking) and not-so-critical (the Ikea website) infrastructure.

For their part, politicians and the spokespeople of affected companies have denied such master plots. And while many presumed that the nationwide airline ground stoppage on 13 November resulted from the Federal Aviation Administration’s rollout of new AI-assisted administration software (called, perhaps aspirationally, the Smart System), the FAA itself laid the blame on a downed router in Arkansas. Microsoft has chalked the recent outage to Outlook not to malicious intrusions, but some buggy code that has been lying dormant for months. Some people will buy such explanations. Others, naturally, may remain skeptical.
Just how worried should we be? Are these disruptions just a new, extremely annoying part of daily life?
points: As tech, travel and banking failures sweep the US, analysts and cyber-security directors discuss AI, underfunding and what keeps them up at night.

articles.title: On Location: Dig Stars Amy Poehler and Geraldine Viswanathan on Italian Gelato, Go-Karting—and Tailgating
articles.summary: The 10-part Peacock series set on an Greek archaeological site found its muse in Italy’s Puglia region.
body: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we take a look at Dig.

Amy Poehler had never been to Greece, but she was immediately entranced by Kate Myers’s novel Excavations about four women coming together for an archaeological dig in Athens. So she took her first trip there to set the scene for her 10-part Peacock comedy series Dig, which drops November 23.

“The way in which Greek people mingle with real antiquities every day, walking past very important structures, is archaeology in process,” the Saturday Night Live alum tells Traveler. “The old and the new are constantly bumping up against each other. It was very cool to be there and really helped remind us of the theme of the show that the past is just around the corner and you can't hide from it.”

articles.title: Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner Reunited at the Paris Theater as The Altruists Hits Netflix
articles.summary: “The first rule of acting is that you don’t judge your character,” Julia Garner told an enthralled audience on Thursday evening at Manhattan’s Paris Theater, moments after the credits rolled following the world premiere of The Altruists.
body: After a screening of the surprisingly humorous pilot episode, Garner and her co-star, Anthony Boyle, joined the show’s creator, Graham Moore, for a panel discussion with actor-turned-journalist Ben McKenzie about the treachery, trickery, and turbulence that pervade the world of cryptocurrency. “You’re probably wondering what’s Ryan Atwood doing up here,” McKenzie joked from the stage, referring to his early-aughts turn as one of The O.C.’s leading teen heartthrobs. “For the last four years, I’ve been investigating and documenting fraud and other criminal activity… And having met and interviewed the real Sam Bankman-Fried, I would like to say that Anthony has a lot more charm [than him].”

After the panel, Garner, in a custom ballet-slipper-pink jumpsuit by Haider Ackermann for Tom Ford and an earful of Lorraine Schwartz bling, and an all-black-clad Boyle joined their castmates, crew members, and press for an after-party in The Plaza Hotel’s Oak Room—making it one of the last industry events to be hosted in the storied venue before it closes for a four-year renovation.

articles.title: Inside the Season’s Best Friendsgiving Parties
articles.summary: Somewhere between Halloween and the holiday party bonanza, Friendsgiving has become fashion’s favorite excuse for a long and unhurried soirée. This year, hosts went all out with candlelit suppers, art gallery takeovers, and apartment hangouts. Here’s a glimpse inside the rooms.
body: The holidays are off to a twinkling start, courtesy of jewelry designer Jessica McCormack and Net-a-Porter. An elegant Friendsgiving dinner saw both parties host a takeover of Salon 94 on the Upper East Side, with a finely decorated table and a mega-watt guest list.

A long table in The Stone Room was lined with low, lush runners of crimson dahlias, burnt-orange chrysanthemums, and inky calla lilies, punctuated by sprays of yellow orchids and tall taper candles. The three-course dinner included sea bass dressed in rainbow carrots, and a dessert of maple pumpkin pie with salted pecan brittle: a seasonal finale worth saving room for.

If there was ever a match made in sartorial heaven, it would be Thom Browne and Mr Porter. To mark the debut of the designer’s exclusive capsule—a seventeen-piece collection of signature knit and quilted styles in festive hues and classic patterns—created in collaboration with the luxury retailer, a debonair group convened at George McNally’s new restaurant Faux in Tribeca.
